questions.question: Which characterisation technique is used to quantify the chemical composition of an unknown sample in conventional SEM and EPMA?
What are the potential artefacts that can arise from sample charging during EPMA analysis of non-conductive alloy phases, and how can these be mitigated?

answers.a: Sample charging improves X-ray production, enhancing analysis
answers.b: Sample charging can lead to beam deflection, localized heating, and distortion of X-ray intensities; mitigate by applying a conductive coating or using low accelerating voltage
answers.c: Sample charging has no significant effect on EPMA analysis
answers.d: Sample charging can be corrected by post-processing the data

questions.question: Why is it necessary to consider the possibility of beam drift during extended EPMA measurements of alloys?

answers.a: Beam drift enhances the spatial resolution; no mitigation is needed
answers.b: Beam drift can cause misalignment of the analysis spot, leading to inaccurate compositional data
answers.c: Beam drift only affects imaging, not compositional analysis
answers.d: Beam drift can be ignored if the beam current is high enough

questions.question: What are the potential challenges in analyzing light elements such as boron (B) and carbon (C) in alloys using EPMA, and how can these challenges be overcome?

answers.a: Light elements have high X-ray emission efficiency; no special techniques are needed
answers.b: Light elements have low X-ray yields and are prone to absorption; overcome by using lower beam energies and applying appropriate ZAF corrections
answers.c: Light elements cause detector saturation; mitigate by using reduced beam currents
answers.d: They are easily ionized; use cryogenic techniques to stabilize the sample

questions.question: How does the surface roughness of an alloy sample impact the accuracy of EPMA analysis, and what methods can be used to minimize these effects?

answers.a: Surface roughness enhances X-ray production; no need for correction
answers.b: Surface roughness can lead to uneven X-ray emission and inaccuracies in composition; mitigate by polishing the sample to a smooth, mirror-like finish
answers.c: Surface roughness only affects imaging, not compositional analysis
answers.d: Surface roughness can be corrected by software algorithms during post-processing
